item.title: HydroJEV: A one-second, training-free screen for cyber-attack and fault attribution in water distribution networks
item.description:
When a SCADA alarm pops up in a water network, operators need to know fast if it’s a cyberattack, a physical fault, a normal glitch or a bad sensor. The authors built Jev, a training‑free model that gives a cause probability in about one second, eliminating the need for labelled data or slow LLMs. Jev achieved competitive accuracy on a four‑class benchmark for the C‑Town water network.

IT Breakdown: If you manage SCADA or OT monitoring, you can add Jev as a first‑pass triage: 1) feed the alarm data into Jev to get instant cause probabilities; 2) use the top suggestion to trigger the appropriate incident response; 3) log the outcome for future training or audit. This reduces manual triage time and improves response accuracy.

item.title: PACE: Provenance-Aware Capability Enforcement for Tool-Using LLM Agents
item.description:
Tool‑using LLM agents can be misdirected by poisoned tool data or memory, leading to unsafe actions. PACE intercepts every tool call, checks its provenance and context before execution, and blocks unsafe calls. This reduces the risk of unintended behaviour in automated systems using LLMs.

IT Breakdown: If you manage cloud infrastructure that runs LLM‑based automation, add a PACE‑style middleware to your tool‑execution pipeline: 1) Log the provenance of each tool (source, version, checksum). 2) Before calling the tool, verify the provenance against an approved catalogue. 3) Block or audit any call that fails the check.

item.title: [News] Gemini 4 Argon: our next era of frontier intelligence
item.description: Google DeepMind has announced the release of Gemini 4 Argon, the latest generation in its frontier intelligence series, featuring advanced multimodal capabilities and real‑time reasoning. The model promises higher accuracy, faster inference, and tighter integration with Google Cloud services.

item.title: [News] Forecasting space weather risks on power grids
item.description: Microsoft Research has developed a machine learning system that forecasts space-weather events, predicting potential damage to power grids and GPS systems 30‑60 minutes before impact.

item.title: [News] Introducing SynthID Bio
item.description: Google DeepMind has unveiled a proof‑of‑concept technology called SynthID Bio that embeds watermarks into AI‑generated proteins without compromising their biological activity. The method uses a neural network to identify and tag sequences, enabling traceability of synthetic biomolecules.
